title: Edge circuit retry hunt — scratchpad
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for the weird client-facing latency spikes on 2026-03-09 that appeared correlated with regional handoffs. This is not the official postmortem — just breadcrumbs & commands I ran while trying to reproduce the failure mode. Keeping raw outputs and quick hypotheses in case it helps the SRE rotation handoff.

Symptoms observed:
- ~04:22–04:48 UTC there were ~30s tail latencies for a subset of requests from eu-west-1 clients that hit the edge gateway.
- Traffic shows many requests with routing decision toggling: primary route -> fallback regional pool -> back to primary within a single request window (seen in route_decision timeline).
- Error surface: 502/504 bursts for 0.6% of tokens in affected window, plus some KV-cache misses that looked correlated.

Correlation IDs / sample traces I pulled:
- cid: f8b2e7a6-3d4b-4a1a-a9b2-0d6c3fe4a2f9 (eu-west-1 client) — timeline shows retry to dedicated pool then fallback, final status 200 but 28s latency.
- cid: 3c9a1f4b-0d2a-4f88-b6d3-2b9fc3f1e6b4 (us-east-1 client routed through eu-west edge) — ended 504.

Commands I ran (most recent first):
- curl to edge router health (timestamped):
  curl -v 'https://edge.redwood.ai/health?region=eu-west-1' -H 'x-rw-cid:f8b2e7a6'
  -> 200 OK (uptime: 23 days). No obvious error.

- grabbed route decision log for cid f8b2e7a6 (kinesis partition):
  aws kinesis get-records --shard-iter <iter> --limit 1000 | jq '.Records[] | select(.Data | contains("f8b2e7a6"))'
  -> found sequence: {"t":1610,..."decision":"primary"} -> {"t":1612,..."decision":"fallback-eu-spot"} -> {"t":1614,..."decision":"primary"}

- sampled proxy logs from edge in pod edge-router-3 (kubectl logs):
  kubectl -n edge logs edge-router-3 --since=2h | grep f8b2e7a6 -A6 -B6
  -> snippet: "upstream handshake timeout after 15000ms" then "retrying to fallback pool"

- queried dedicated pool API for instance health:
  curl -s 'https://internal.dedicated.svc/pools/eu-west-1/health' | jq
  -> most instances healthy but 2/12 reported high inflight (qps spike around 04:20 UTC).

- KV-cache telemetry check (redis cluster metrics):
  redis-cli -h cache-eu-1 info stats | egrep 'keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses|instantaneous_ops'
  -> during window misses jumped ~3x and ops spiked; suggests sudden cache churn.

Error snippets saved:
- "upstream handshake timeout after 15000ms"
- "connection reset by peer during prefix replay"
- HTTP/2: "RST_STREAM code=2" in proxy->inference logs

Hypotheses (quick):
1) Inference backend instances (dedicated) experienced transient GC or driver stalls under a QPS spike -> proxy retried to fallback pool; during handshake the client waited and got long tail.
2) Regional egress issue: some AZs saw packet drops causing TLS handshake retransmits and RST_STREAM; router interpreted these as backend unreachability and applied fallback policy repeatedly.
3) KV-cache coldness after a period of churn (evictions) caused longer prefix recompute, lengthening backend load and causing timeouts.
4) Routing policy TTL bug: decision TTL set to 0 in certain error cases -> router flaps between pools within 2–3s windows.

Quick reproduction notes I attempted locally:
- Simulated slow backend with `tc qdisc` on a staging node to add 250ms delay to backend responses. Saw similar long tails but not the rapid decision flapping.
- Created a script to hammer KV cache with high-variance prefixes to force evictions; observed higher backend CPU due to prefix recompute.

Immediate next steps (TODO for triage):
- [ ] Pull kernel and nvidia-driver dmesg on the two dedicated instances that reported high inflight; look for OOM or GPU resets.
- [ ] Re-run k8s pod-level tcpdump on edge-router-3 for 04:10–04:30 window (requires coordination; historian snapshot might exist).
- [ ] Add temporary sampling on route decision TTL to log TTL values for decisions in next 24h.
- [ ] Correlate infra network metrics (vpc flow logs) for candidate AZs at window.

Playbook fragment to chase similar incidents quickly:
1) Get CID from customer: run kinesis grep -> collect route decision timeline and proxy logs.
2) Check dedicated pool health and inflight per-instance around timestamps.
3) Inspect KV-cache miss/eviction rates; check for prefix recompute spikes.
4) If handshake timeouts present: do tcpdump + check kernel logs + driver resets. If RST_STREAM: check HTTP/2 connection reuse and maxConcurrentStreams throttles.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Was there a config push around 04:00 UTC? (asked infra, awaiting reply).
- How aggressive is our router TTL when encountering consecutive handshakes failures? Could that TTL be 0 in a bug path?
- Need to make a lightweight probe that simulates the exact 3-stage flow (primary -> fallback -> primary) to see if router keeps a sticky backoff.

Raw artifacts saved locally:
- /tmp/edge-f8b2e7a6-proxy.log (partial), /tmp/redis-stats-2026-03-09-04-30.json, /tmp/dedicated-instance-ids.txt

If anyone picks this up: ping me (Marisol) in #sre-rotation and paste CID f8b2e7a6. I'll forward the tcpdump creds and the instance IDs.

End of scratchpad — will convert to incident timeline if more signals confirm a definitive root cause.
